trends.name: Lefty: A Left-Spiral Pour-Over Brewer
trends.buzz: A new stainless steel pour-over brewer called Lefty, shaped as a left-hand spiral, has made its debut.
trends.angle: New shapes, new fun — if you love tinkering with pour-over, this spiral design is worth a look no matter your experience level. Brewing is brewing, there's no 'right' dripper.'

trends.name: Going Big on the V60: 30g+ Recipe
trends.buzz: Lance Hedrick shares a new approach for brewing big batches (30g+) on the V60, while noting 15-18g doses are still his favorite — and he skips stirring.
trends.angle: Whether you brew 15g or 30g, there's no wrong dose. Try this recipe if you've been curious about bigger V60 brews for groups or refills.

trends.name: A $320 'Endgame' Pour-Over Setup
trends.buzz: DaddyGotCoffee lays out a pour-over kit — 1Zpresso ZP6 grinder, Hario Switch, CAFEC filters — that he says gets you 85-90% of the way to an endgame setup for about $320.
trends.angle: Great gear doesn't have to mean a bottomless budget. This is a welcoming starting point for anyone ready to level up their home pour-over without breaking the bank.

trends.name: xBloom Studio: Grinder + Scale + Brewer in One
trends.buzz: The xBloom Studio combines a grinder, scale, and pour-over brewer into one machine, giving full control over grind, water temp, and pour pattern.
trends.angle: All-in-one brewers are a great option for anyone who wants pour-over quality without juggling five gadgets — no gatekeeping on how you get your cup.

trends.name: Timemore's New Lineup at Lujiazui Coffee Festival
trends.buzz: Brian Quan previews Timemore's new gear at their Shanghai festival booth, including the C6 and S5 hand grinders, Delta Switch, 064 Gen II Sculptor, and Finca espresso machine.
trends.angle: Lots of fresh options across price points coming from Timemore — exciting news whether you're hand-grinding at home or eyeing your first espresso machine.

trends.name: The Cappuccino You Can Eat
trends.buzz: James Hoffmann built an actual edible 'Cappuccino Pie,' layering pastry, coffee, and foam into a dessert version of the classic drink.
trends.angle: Coffee doesn't have to stay in the cup — this is the kind of playful experiment that reminds us specialty coffee can be fun, not just serious ritual.

trends.name: Nespresso Pod Shrinkflation Rumors
trends.buzz: Reddit users are alleging Nespresso may be putting less coffee into their pods, sparking frustration online.
trends.angle: We haven't confirmed this ourselves, but it's a good reminder to check what you're actually getting in any pod or bag — worth watching before drawing conclusions.

trends.name: Is Oat Milk Still the Default?
trends.buzz: Blue Bottle's switch back to whole milk signals oat milk's long run as specialty coffee's default may be softening, even as it keeps growing in Europe.
trends.angle: Dairy, oat, or anything in between — your milk choice is yours. This trend shift is interesting, not a verdict on what's 'correct' in your cup.

trends.name: Home Machines Want to Act More Like Cafés
trends.buzz: Home coffee drinkers increasingly want café-style control — adjustable strength, temperature, milk type — pushing super-automatic machines to add more personalization.
trends.angle: Whatever your setup, more control over your cup is a win. Great to see machines meeting people where they are instead of demanding they upgrade their whole routine.

trends.name: Single-Dose vs. Hopper Grinders, Live
trends.buzz: Whole Latte Love is hosting a livestream comparing single-dose and hopper-fed grinders, covering burr types, grind adjustments, and dialing-in tips.
trends.angle: No grinder style is 'better' — it's about what fits your routine. A good resource if you're trying to pick your first (or next) grinder without the overwhelm.

trends.name: Coffee Delivered by Bike, Van, and Dinghy
trends.buzz: Seattle's new Barometer Coffee is delivering roasted coffee to customers' doors — and to boats along the waterways — by bike, van, and even dinghy.
trends.angle: Love seeing creative, low-key ways roasters reach their community. Specialty coffee can show up anywhere, not just behind a counter.

trends.name: Fruit-Forward Co-Ferments Meet Milk Drinks
trends.buzz: Roasters are experimenting with fruit-forward, co-fermented coffees in milk-based drinks, using sourcing and roast adjustments to create distinctive flavor without added syrups.
trends.angle: A fun way to explore flavor if you're curious about going beyond the usual latte — no syrup required, just thoughtful sourcing and roasting.
